features.title: Agent preview browser
features.summary: Agent tools drive a headless Chromium on the DSH Host, one isolated browser context per thread: preview_open, preview_navigate, preview_snapshot (bounded accessibility text with element refs), preview_screenshot (image), preview_click, preview_type, preview_evaluate (off until the user enables it), preview_reveal, preview_close and preview_list. Top-level navigations are limited to allowed hosts, loopback by default. A thread's pages close after it idles or when it is disposed, and preview_open with reveal (or preview_reveal) shows the URL in the user's browser tab beside the thread.
failureModes: A top-level navigation to a host outside allowedHosts is refused before loading, and a link or redirect to one is aborted in the browser.
Chromium missing or failing to launch reports how to install the headless shell or set chromiumPath instead of a stack trace.
A snapshot ref from an older snapshot that no longer resolves fails the action with a timeout that asks for a fresh preview_snapshot.
An agent cannot act on another thread's pages; a Client must name the thread.
preview_evaluate stays refused until the user turns on allowEvaluate.

externalDependencies.boundary: Launches one headless Chromium per Host over a pipe (no debugging port), creates one context per thread without downloads or service workers, and drives pages on loopback dev servers.

features.title: Thread dev servers
features.summary: The thread header shows a chip with the TCP ports a thread's processes listen on — processes from its jobs or bash calls, and processes running inside its workspace — plus its open preview pages. Each row opens its URL in the browser tab beside the thread or stops the server (a live job through the job registry, otherwise SIGTERM then SIGKILL on that exact process). thread_dev_servers and thread_dev_server_stop give the agent the same list and stop.
failureModes: The DSH Host and the processes that launched it are never listed, so their ports can never be stopped from here.
A pid recycled between the list and the stop is refused because the stop re-reads the process table and matches pid and start time.
Several threads sharing one checkout all list a server no job attributes; the job owner wins when a job matches.
Listening sockets no thread accounts for (other apps, system services) are not listed.
Open is disabled when no browser tab is available beside the thread on screen.

externalDependencies.boundary: Read-only current-user listening sockets, process table and working directories through the Host subprocess service; the only writes are the confirmed stop of one listed server.

features.title: Offline HTML screenshots for other Host plugins
features.summary: The preview-render dshx contract (@dshfiles/preview/render-api) lets another Host plugin screenshot an untrusted HTML document in the preview Chromium: a fresh offline browser context per call with every request aborted, the document in an allow-scripts, opaque-origin srcdoc frame, an optional full-page capture up to 6000 pixels, and a JPEG returned as base64 within the API payload budget. Only plugin callers are served; html-render's html_render_screenshot is the agent tool over it.
failureModes: A Client or Agent caller is refused: the contract serves other Host plugins only.
An image that stays above the budget at every JPEG quality is refused with how to shrink the capture.
A missing browser fails like every preview tool, naming the install command and the chromiumPath setting.

externalDependencies.boundary: One Host Chromium launched over the pipe transport; each render gets its own offline context that is closed after the capture.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: Unit tests render against the real headless shell with a loopback server that counts requests, proving none leave the context.
